unit.why: A homily from the book ל"מ on Yitro contains a first-person memorate: the author spent Sukkot with the Seer of Lublin and watched him bless the lulav.
unit.boundary_note: The narrative is wrapped in an extended homiletic frame (exegesis of Exodus 20).

stories.start_quote: כאשר אירע לי בעצמי פ״א חגגתי
stories.end_quote: ואין לשער מדרגתו הגדולה בשעת הברכה
stories.summary_en: The author spent Sukkot in Lublin with R. Jacob Isaac, the Seer. The crowd imitated the Seer's trembling before the lulav blessing. The author sat apart and waited, then closely watched the blessing itself, whose exalted level he found beyond estimation; the homily draws the lesson that one should look to a tzaddik's inner worship, as Moses did at Sinai.
